$comment: Parameters passed on the stack AFTER a stacked aggregate, and an aggregate stacked after stacked scalars (D-MIR-STACKED-SCALAR-AFTER-A-STACKED-AGGREGATE-REFUSED). Once the argument registers run out, a by-value struct, an x87 `long double` (x86_64 SysV always stacks it) or an AAPCS64 `_Complex long double` takes its bytes in the stack area and the scalars after it follow; each function checks every parameter against a distinct value and has its own exit code (11–19, listed in `main.c`). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-19: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 run it to 42 at -O0 and -O2 on x86_64 and aarch64 Linux; the P68 round-7 base refused the callee of every shape on the Linux target whose registers run out. ★ The `release` arm: every call goes through a `volatile` function pointer, so the optimized pipeline keeps the argument passing real.
